title: VPC Hardening Playbook — Network Defenses, RBAC v2 & Audit Export
content:
Purpose:
This playbook consolidates recommended network hardening patterns, RBAC v2 mappings for control-plane components, a compact audit-log schema for Private deployments, and a practical SIEM export map. It also includes a minimal evidence-automation runbook to produce artifacts that satisfy common compliance reviews. Intended audience: SREs running Private/VPC deployments, security engineers validating customer evidence, and the solutions-engineering team preparing customer handoffs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood Private control plane and customer-managed inference clusters running inside customer VPCs or connected VPCs via transit gateways.
- Assumes use of cloud-managed networking (AWS/GCP/Azure) with standard security groups / cloud firewall primitives.
- mTLS described is mutual-auth between service peers (control-plane <-> runtime, router <-> model-worker). Keys managed by customer KMS/HSM where required.

High-level patterns (quick):
1) Zero-exposure control plane: control-plane admin endpoints only reachable from bastion or specific mgmt CIDRs via ALB/private NLB. No public IPs.
2) Service segmentation: per-role subnets (control, runtime, metrics, prov) + security group allow lists by tag.
3) Strong egress controls: default-deny egress with explicit destinations for telemetry, updates, and registry pulls.
4) mTLS everywhere for cluster-internal RPCs; TLS for external customer-facing endpoints.
5) Immutable evidence snapshot: automated daily export of audit logs + cert inventory to object storage with retention metadata.

Network diagrams (ASCII):
[Customer-VPC]--(Transit-GW)--[Redwood-VPC:control-subnet]
                           |\n                           +- [runtime-subnet] -> model-workers (mTLS)
                           |\n                           +- [metrics-subnet] -> prometheus, opensearch (restricted)

Firewall rule guidance (example primitives):
- Control-plane NLB (internal): allow TCP 443 from management CIDR, allow health-checks from ALB-sg. Deny all else.
- Router -> Worker: allow TCP 9000-9010 (gRPC ranges) from router-sg to worker-sg, source verified by mTLS.
- Metrics ingestion: allow Prometheus scrape from monitoring-gw only, port 9090.
- Egress to model registry: allow TLS 443 to registry FQNs/IPs; leverage private endpoints where possible.

Security group example (AWS-like):
- sg-control-plane: inbound {443 from 10.10.0.0/24 (ops-bastion)} outbound {0.0.0.0/0 limited by NACL}
- sg-router: inbound {9000-9010 from sg-control-plane} outbound {9000-9010 to sg-workers}
- sg-workers: inbound {9000-9010 from sg-router} outbound {443 to registry, 443 to logging}

mTLS recommendations and rotation:
- Mutual TLS issued by an internal CA (customer-owned) with a 90-day short-lived leaf policy. Use automations (cert-manager or internal tooling) to rotate transparently.
- Certificate inventories must be exported daily with subject, SANs, thumbprint, notBefore/notAfter.
- For bootstrapping in air-gapped installs: pre-seed leaf certs + store CA root in HSM.
- Failure mode: if mTLS validation fails, fallback is not allowed; the control-plane must reject and emit audit event AUTH.MTLS.FAIL with reason.

RBAC v2 model (concise):
- Roles: infra-admin, infra-operator, runtime-operator, audit-reader, customer-admin (scoped to customer resources).
- Principals: service-identity (system:router), user (email), api-key.
- Permission primitives: read:list, read:get, write:create, write:update, exec, admin.
- Resource types: cluster, deployment, model-worker, secret, audit-log, evidence-bundle.

Example role binding (plain text):
role: runtime-operator
permissions: [write:create, write:update, exec]
scopes: [cluster:customer-123, deployment:*]
bound-to: group:infra-operators@example.com

Audit log schema (single-line JSON per event - newline-delimited JSON):
{ "ts":"2026-02-14T15:12:03Z", "event_id":"evt_01F0XK", "principal":"service:router-01", "principal_type":"service", "action":"rpc.execute", "resource":"model-worker/worker-019", "result":"denied", "reason":"mTLS_failed", "request_id":"req_9a2f", "trace_id":"trace-xyz", "ctx":{ "src_ip":"10.10.3.45", "user_agent":"router/1.3.0" } }
Fields explained: ts, event_id, principal, principal_type, action (namespace.verb), resource, result (success|denied|error), reason (short token), request_id, trace_id, ctx (free-form kv pairs).

SIEM export mapping (recommended fields for Splunk/Elastic):
- timestamp -> ts
- host -> resource (normalize to host or worker id)
- identity -> principal
- action -> action
- outcome -> result
- outcome_reason -> reason
- trace -> trace_id
- request -> request_id
- extras -> ctx (flattened)
Export tips: use structured JSON ingestion (no multiline). Tag each record with deployment_id and env. Add index-time enrichers to map principal to human owner using HR/group sync table.

Evidence automation runbook (daily snapshot):
1) Export audit logs for last 24h: aws s3 cp s3://customer-audit-bucket/logs/$(date -I) audit-logs/$(date -I).jsonl
2) Pull cert inventory via API: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVID_TOKEN" https://controlplane.local/api/v1/certs > certs-$(date -I).json
3) Generate short summary (sha256) and manifest.json listing filenames, sizes, and retention tags.
4) Upload to evidence store with immutable flag (object lock) and record a ticket JIRA-PD-XXXXX for audit consumption.

Minimal automation script snippet (bash, conceptual):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
DAY=$(date -I)
mkdir -p /tmp/evidence/$DAY
aws s3 cp s3://customer-audit-bucket/logs/$DAY /tmp/evidence/$DAY/audit.jsonl
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVID_TOKEN" https://controlplane.local/api/v1/certs > /tmp/evidence/$DAY/certs.json
sha256sum /tmp/evidence/$DAY/* > /tmp/evidence/$DAY/manifest.sha256
aws s3 cp --acl bucket-owner-full-control --storage-class STANDARD_IA /tmp/evidence/$DAY/ s3://customer-evidence-bucket/$DAY/ --recursive

Hardening checklist (deployment run):
- [ ] Control-plane endpoints restricted to management CIDRs (no public access)
- [ ] All inter-service traffic authenticated via mTLS
- [ ] Security groups follow least-privilege (no /0 opens except for known egress proxies)
- [ ] Egress filter lists configured and justified in change doc
- [ ] RBAC v2 roles defined and mapped for operators before cutover
- [ ] Audit export pipeline validated (jsonl format, 24h window) and ingests into SIEM
- [ ] Evidence automation scheduled and smoke-tested for restores
- [ ] Cert rotation automation enabled and short-lived leaf cert policy active

Operational runbook (on incident):
- If audit export pipeline fails: check S3 permissions, check control-plane token validity, restart exporter pod, escalate to infra-operator.
- If mTLS handshakes start failing cluster-wide: collect recent audit events AUTH.MTLS.FAIL, export cert inventory, consult CA logs, and isolate new certs by thumbprint.
- For suspicious SIEM alert (audit-log tampering): immediately snapshot current logs + object-store list, freeze evidence bucket (object-lock), notify compliance and open a security incident.

References and links:
- Internal confluence: CONFLUENCE-12345 (detailed RBAC v2 design)
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/678 (firewall rules templates)
- Runbook ticket template: JIRA-PD-3421

Open questions / decision points:
- Decide on default cert lifetime for air-gapped deployments (proposed: 180 days for leaf if rotation automation not available).
- Approve list of external egress endpoints for model registry (req: security review).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an operational playbook draft: expect iterative updates as we onboard first enterprise private deployment. Where possible, prefer private endpoints and customer KMS.
- Feedback requested on whether RBAC role names align with customer IAM mappings (we will supply a mapping script for major clouds).

Last reviewed by: Ava Morales on 2026-02-15
